title: CostLedgerV1
description: Every token, dollar, and millisecond an agent run spent, itemized per step and totalled. Persisted alongside the trace and aggregated per eval run; cost per correct answer is derived from these. Accounting is built in from the first commit because retrofitting it is how you end up without it.

run_id.description: Identifier of the agent run this ledger belongs to

price_table_date.description: The date the price table used for these dollar figures was last verified, as ISO 8601. Prices live in versioned config, never inline, so a stale table is visible rather than silent.

entries.description: One entry per step that consumed tokens or time

step.description: Index of the trace event this charge belongs to

tokens_in.description: Input tokens as reported by the provider, not estimated

tokens_out.description: Output tokens as reported by the provider

usd.description: Dollars for this step, computed from the versioned price table

cost_known.description: False when the provider closed the stream without reporting usage. The runtime never estimates token counts, so such a step has an unknown cost, not a zero one — tokens_in, tokens_out and usd are then all 0 and carry no meaning. A reader that ignores this flag will report a paid step as free.

cache_hit.description: True when the semantic cache served this step and no provider call was made

escalated.description: True when this step ran on the expensive tier because the router escalated

repair_depth.description: Repair iteration this step belongs to; 0 is the first attempt

usd.description: Sum of entry dollars. The per-question budget cap is enforced against this value as it grows, not after the fact.

provider_calls.description: Number of steps that actually hit a provider, i.e. entries with cache_hit false

steps_cost_unknown.description: How many entries have cost_known false. When this is above zero the totals above are a LOWER BOUND, not the cost of the run, and anything deriving cost per correct answer has to say so.
